stories.headline: Eddie Rommel Wins 27th Game, Leads American League

image.alt: Black-and-white photo of a ballplayer in road uniform with glove, dugout setting

stories.extract: Edwin Americus Rommel was an American baseball player, coach, and umpire who played as a right-handed pitcher and in Major League Baseball. He spent his entire playing career (1920–1932) with the Philadelphia Athletics. He is considered to be one of the earlier adaptors of the modern knuckleball.

stories.text: Washington Senators first baseman Ed Cartwright hits for the cycle against the Boston Beaneaters.
stories.headline: Ed Cartwright Hits for the Cycle Against Boston Beaneaters

image.alt: Man in cap and large W-lettered knit sweater, studio portrait, vintage

stories.extract: Edward Charles "Jumbo" Cartwright was an American professional baseball first baseman who played in the major leagues in 1890 and from 1894 to 1897. He played for the St. Louis Browns of the American Association and the Washington Senators of the National League.

stories.text: The Chicago White Stockings accept the challenge issued by the St. Louis Browns to play a World Championship Series. The teams agree on a best-of-7 game format with the winner taking the entire gate money from the series.
stories.headline: White Stockings Accept Browns' Challenge for Championship Series

stories.text: The last place Cincinnati Stars win their final game 2–0 in front of 183 fans. This will be the last game for this troubled franchise, although the city will see the current version of the Reds begin play in 1882.
stories.headline: Cincinnati Stars Win Final Game 2-0 Before 183 Fans
stories.extract: The Cincinnati Stars were a Major League Baseball team that played in the National League for the 1880 season and were managed by John Clapp. The club finished their only season in 8th place with a record of 21–59.

stories.text: The National League completes its schedule, marking the first time in professional baseball that a full schedule has been played by all member teams.
